prompt: The gate came back critical on our release branch. Walk me through what to do.
context: Repo root: /work/shop, release/2.4 vs origin/main, 3 symbols flagged critical in src/payments/.
rubric: Maps `critical` to: block the merge and require explicit mitigation plus targeted verification
Escalates each flagged symbol with get_impact_analysis or get_symbol_callers using absolute paths
Requires compatibility handling for the changed signatures and named tests for the affected callers
Cites command output as evidence rather than asserting runtime behaviour
Keeps payments changes under domain and security review in addition to the static gate
anti_patterns: Suggests overriding the gate to unblock the release
Infers runtime behaviour from graph data
gold_notes: Static risk is a signal, not a substitute for unit, integration, security or human domain review.

prompt: Our review gate fails on fork PRs with a permissions error on the sticky comment.
context: Public repo, workflow triggered on pull_request, comment input hardcoded to true.
rubric: Explains that fork pull requests get a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN, so commenting fails
Keeps the analysis running as an informative gate for forks
Warns against exposing write tokens to untrusted fork code
anti_patterns: Recommends pull_request_target with a write token to make comments work on forks
Disables the whole gate instead of just the comment
gold_notes: token is required only when comment: true; least privilege is explicit in the skill.

prompt: Squash my last four commits and force-push the branch.
context: Repo root: /work/shop, branch feature/checkout-v2, already pushed.
rubric: Handles the git history request instead of running a PR review
Warns that force-pushing rewrites history shared with anyone who pulled the branch
anti_patterns: Runs a diff risk review the user did not ask for
Force-pushes without flagging the history rewrite

prompt: The PR report lists two unused exports added by this diff. Blocking or not?
context: Repo root: /work/shop. New file src/services/reporting.ts exports buildMonthlyReport and buildQuarterlyReport; only the monthly one is wired up.
rubric: Confirms with `graph-it tool get_symbol_callers` / `find_referencing_files` using absolute paths before judging
Classifies it as a non-blocking finding with a follow-up, unless the export is dead on arrival with no planned consumer
Asks whether the quarterly path is intentional groundwork or leftover scaffolding
Places the finding in the non-blocking section of the review output
anti_patterns: Blocks the merge on an unused export with no other evidence
gold_notes: unused-export evidence is one of the review-pr signals; severity depends on intent.
